summary: A history of the swastika, an ancient good-luck symbol used from prehistoric Ukraine to India and the Navajo, and how 19th-century Aryan race theory and occultists led the Nazis to seize it, with the fallout for Hindu, Buddhist, Jain and Native users today.

evidence.note: oldest known swastika pattern on a mammoth-ivory figurine from Mezine, dated about 15,000 years ago
Navajo whirling log symbol and its ritual use in sand paintings introduced
Schliemann segment begins; Troy dig and swastika pottery finds in 1868 onward
Troy swastikas read as proof of an Aryan root race by European race theorists
US trading posts commercialise the symbol on Navajo silver; national swastika product craze
Lanz von Liebenfels, Order of the New Templars, Ostara and his swastika flag at Castle Werfenstein
Freikorps use in 1919 and Nazi Party adoption in 1920
1933 Nazi law restricting commercial use of the symbol
town of Swastika, Ontario resists wartime renaming
India: Hindu use, Savitri Devi, Indian Nazi party and Hitler-branded businesses
post-Soviet far right, US bikers, punks and White Aryan Resistance revive the symbol
2022 disputes over Diwali decorations, California law and reclaiming the symbol

notes: No subject kind for a symbol; practice-or-pseudoscience is the closest fit. Story spans ~13,000 BCE (Mezine figurine) to 2022, but the schema floor is -5000, so covered_span.start is clamped. Origin IN (Sanskrit word) and UA (oldest find) are judgement calls for a symbol. Secondary 'Nazi Party' could be split into Thule Society/Freikorps. Hosts treat no single person as the bastard; no roles apply.
